clinical_category: Adult pneumococcal vaccination - current age-based prevention recommendation
stem: A 52-year-old adult who has never received a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine asks about pneumococcal vaccination. Which response by the nurse is accurate according to current CDC recommendations?

options.A: CDC recommends pneumococcal vaccination for adults age 50 years or older; the available vaccines protect against specific pneumococcal serotypes rather than every possible cause of pneumonia
options.B: Routine pneumococcal vaccination does not begin until age 75 unless the client works in health care
options.C: Pneumococcal vaccination guarantees prevention of all bacterial and viral pneumonias
options.D: Pneumococcal vaccination is recommended only after a person develops chronic lung disease

rationale: A is correct. CDC's current 2026 pneumococcal guidance recommends pneumococcal vaccination for all adults age 50 years or older who have not previously received an indicated pneumococcal conjugate vaccine or whose vaccination history is unknown. CDC also explains that individual pneumococcal vaccines protect against specific serotypes of pneumococcal bacteria; they do not prevent every cause of pneumonia. B uses an incorrect age threshold. C overstates vaccine protection. D is incorrect because age 50 years or older is itself a current routine indication, although certain younger adults also qualify based on risk conditions.
educational_objective: Teach adults that current CDC guidance recommends pneumococcal vaccination beginning at age 50 years for those who need it, and that pneumococcal vaccines protect against specific pneumococcal serotypes rather than all causes of pneumonia.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Pneumococcal Vaccine Recommendations; Recommended Vaccines for Adults; Types of Pneumococcal Vaccines
source_version_date: CDC pneumococcal guidance updated 2026-02-25; current at access 2026-08-18
source_locator: CDC 'Pneumococcal Vaccine Recommendations' → Key Points and 'Adults 50 years or older': CDC recommends pneumococcal vaccination for adults 50 years or older; administer an indicated PCV to adults in this age group who have never received a PCV or whose history is unknown. CDC 'Types of Pneumococcal Vaccines' → Key Points: pneumococcal vaccines differ in the serotypes or strains they protect against; each vaccine protects against specific pneumococcal serotypes.
source_claim_supported: Current February 2026 CDC guidance directly supports routine age-based pneumococcal vaccination beginning at age 50 and the statement that vaccine protection is serotype-specific rather than protection against every cause of pneumonia.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests adult preventive-health teaching and immunization recommendations.
correction_summary: Substantive currentness rebuild. The source item used generic 'older adult' wording and a generic CDC vaccine URL. Current CDC guidance changed the routine adult age-based recommendation to age 50 years or older. The final item uses the exact February 2026 recommendation and avoids claiming prevention of all pneumonia etiologies or prescribing a vaccine sequence without the client's full vaccination history.
audit_findings: The generic CDC vaccine URL did not provide an exact current recommendation locator.
CDC guidance updated February 25, 2026 directly recommends pneumococcal vaccination for adults age 50 years or older who need an indicated PCV.
The final item incorporates the current age threshold rather than outdated older-adult-only wording.
The answer explicitly limits vaccine protection to specific pneumococcal serotypes and excludes the false claim that all pneumonias are prevented.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no unnecessary vaccine-sequence precision, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
